plan: Eliminate all leveraged ETFs to reduce volatility.
Significantly reduce broad index (SPY) to meet concentration mandate.
Increase allocation to income-focused QQQI for stability.
Trim concentrated tech (CRWD) to manage risk.
Add a high-quality tech name (MSFT) for diversification.
Maintain a substantial cash buffer for capital preservation.
conservative.read: This plan prioritizes capital preservation with lower volatility. Expect modest monthly gains around 1.5% with reduced drawdown potential. Significant cash holdings will dampen upside.

plan: Reduce exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to manage risk.
Trim broad index (SPY) to meet the single name concentration limit.
Reduce concentration in high-growth tech (CRWD).
Add a high-quality tech name (MSFT) for diversification.
Introduce a high risk/reward setup (PLTR) for growth potential.
Maintain a moderate cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced approach aims for risk-first growth, targeting around 2.5% monthly. It blends broad market exposure with quality tech and selective high-potential names. Leverage is kept low, but concentration risk is reduced.

plan: Increase allocation to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) for amplified gains.
Add to strong performing tech (CRWD) to press winners.
Introduce new high-conviction scanner setups (MSFT, PLTR, IONQ).
Concentrate exposure in highest-scoring names.
Maintain a smaller cash buffer to maximize invested capital.
Utilize wider but strict stops to manage increased risk.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan seeks high growth, targeting around 4% monthly, but carries significantly higher risk. Increased leverage and concentration amplify both gains and potential losses. Leveraged ETFs have daily decay, and drawdowns can be severe.

plan: Eliminate all leveraged and high-beta single name positions.
Maximize allocation to income-focused QQQI for steady distributions.
Reduce broad index (SPY) to increase cash buffer.
Add exposure to the financial sector (XLF) for diversification.
Prioritize low drawdown and reliable monthly income.
Accept lower growth potential in exchange for stability.
income.read: This income-focused plan prioritizes stable monthly distributions and capital preservation, targeting around 1% monthly. It significantly reduces volatility by cutting leverage and growth stocks. NAV can still decline in market downturns, and distributions are not guaranteed.
